concepts.name: Real Numbers
concepts.description: The real number system includes rational numbers (integers, fractions, terminating and repeating decimals) and irrational numbers (non-terminating, non-repeating decimals such as √2 and π). Students place real numbers on the number line and compare their magnitudes.

concepts.name: Integer Operations
concepts.description: Addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division of positive and negative integers. Includes the rules for signs, the concept of additive inverses, and order of operations (PEMDAS/BODMAS).

concepts.name: Fraction and Decimal Operations
concepts.description: Addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division of fractions and decimals. Converting between fraction, decimal, and percent forms. Finding least common denominators.

concepts.name: Properties of Operations
concepts.description: Commutative, associative, distributive, and identity properties of addition and multiplication. Applying properties to simplify arithmetic and algebraic expressions.

concepts.name: Exponents and Square Roots
concepts.description: Integer exponents and their properties (product rule, quotient rule, power rule, zero exponent, negative exponent). Square roots and cube roots of perfect squares/cubes. Simplifying radical expressions.

concepts.name: Variables and Algebraic Expressions
concepts.description: Using letters as variables to represent unknown quantities. Writing, reading, and evaluating algebraic expressions. Understanding coefficients, terms, and constants.

concepts.name: Combining Like Terms
concepts.description: Identifying like terms (same variable and exponent). Adding and subtracting like terms to simplify polynomial expressions. The concept of equivalence between expressions.

concepts.name: Evaluating Algebraic Expressions
concepts.description: Substituting numerical values for variables and computing the result. Using order of operations with variables. Evaluating multi-variable expressions.

concepts.name: Writing Algebraic Expressions from Word Problems
concepts.description: Translating verbal descriptions into algebraic expressions. Keywords such as 'sum,' 'difference,' 'product,' 'quotient,' 'less than,' and 'more than.' Setting up expressions for real-world contexts.

concepts.name: Solving One-Step Equations
concepts.description: Using inverse operations (addition/subtraction, multiplication/division) to isolate the variable. The concept of equality: what you do to one side you must do to the other. Checking solutions.

concepts.name: Solving Two-Step Equations
concepts.description: Solving equations requiring two inverse operations (e.g., 2x + 3 = 11). Strategy: undo addition/subtraction first, then multiplication/division. Writing and solving from word problems.

concepts.name: Solving Multi-Step Equations
concepts.description: Equations requiring the distributive property and combining like terms before isolating the variable. Variables on both sides. Equations with fractions and decimals as coefficients.
aliases: equations with variables on both sides

concepts.name: Literal Equations and Formulas
concepts.description: Solving equations for a specified variable in terms of others (e.g., solve A = lw for l). Rearranging familiar formulas such as the distance formula, area formulas, and the slope formula.

concepts.name: Solving Linear Inequalities
concepts.description: Solving single-variable linear inequalities. Graphing solution sets on a number line. The rule for flipping the inequality symbol when multiplying or dividing by a negative number. Compound inequalities (AND/OR).

concepts.name: The Coordinate Plane
concepts.description: Plotting ordered pairs (x, y) in the four quadrants. Identifying quadrant, x-intercept, and y-intercept. Distance between points in special cases (horizontal or vertical lines).

concepts.name: Rate of Change and Slope
concepts.description: Slope as the ratio of vertical change to horizontal change (rise/run). Calculating slope from two points using the slope formula m = (y₂ - y₁)/(x₂ - x₁). Interpreting slope as a unit rate in context. Positive, negative, zero, and undefined slope.

concepts.name: Slope-Intercept Form
concepts.description: The equation y = mx + b: slope m and y-intercept b. Graphing a line from slope-intercept form. Writing the equation of a line from a graph. Identifying the y-intercept as the starting value.

concepts.name: Point-Slope Form
concepts.description: Writing the equation of a line in point-slope form y - y₁ = m(x - x₁) given the slope and a point. Converting between point-slope and slope-intercept forms. Writing equations given two points.

concepts.name: Standard Form of a Linear Equation
concepts.description: The standard form Ax + By = C. Rewriting equations in standard form. Finding x- and y-intercepts from standard form and using them to graph the line.

concepts.name: Parallel and Perpendicular Lines
concepts.description: Parallel lines have equal slopes; perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals (m₁ × m₂ = -1). Writing equations of lines parallel or perpendicular to a given line through a given point.

concepts.name: Introduction to Functions
concepts.description: Definition of a function: each input has exactly one output. Function notation f(x). Domain and range. Determining whether a relation is a function using the vertical line test. Input-output tables.

concepts.name: Linear Functions
concepts.description: Recognizing linear functions from tables, graphs, and equations. The relationship between linear functions and constant rate of change. Comparing linear functions represented in different forms.

concepts.name: Arithmetic Sequences
concepts.description: Identifying arithmetic sequences by a constant common difference. Writing explicit (aₙ = a₁ + (n-1)d) and recursive rules for arithmetic sequences. Connecting arithmetic sequences to linear functions.

concepts.name: Solving Systems by Graphing
concepts.description: A system of two linear equations has one solution (intersection point), no solution (parallel lines), or infinitely many solutions (same line). Graphing both lines and identifying the solution from the intersection.

concepts.name: Solving Systems by Substitution
concepts.description: The substitution method: solve one equation for one variable, substitute into the other equation. Solving the resulting single-variable equation. Back-substituting to find the second variable. Checking solutions.

concepts.name: Solving Systems by Elimination
concepts.description: The elimination (addition/linear combination) method: multiply equations by constants so that one variable cancels when equations are added. Solving for the remaining variable, then back-substituting.

concepts.name: Systems of Equations — Word Problems
concepts.description: Modeling real-world situations with a system of two equations (e.g., mixture problems, rate problems, cost problems). Choosing an efficient method (substitution or elimination). Interpreting the solution in context.

concepts.name: Introduction to Polynomials
concepts.description: Vocabulary: monomial, binomial, trinomial, polynomial; degree of a term and polynomial; leading coefficient. Standard (descending) form. Classifying polynomials by degree and number of terms.

concepts.name: Adding and Subtracting Polynomials
concepts.description: Adding polynomials by combining like terms. Subtracting polynomials by distributing the negative sign and combining like terms. Arranging results in standard form.

concepts.name: Multiplying Polynomials
concepts.description: Multiplying a monomial by a polynomial using the distributive property. Multiplying two binomials using FOIL (First, Outer, Inner, Last) or the distributive property. Multiplying a binomial by a trinomial. Special products: (a+b)², (a-b)², (a+b)(a-b).

concepts.name: Factoring: Greatest Common Factor
concepts.description: Finding the greatest common factor (GCF) of a polynomial's terms. Factoring out the GCF to write a polynomial as a product. Recognizing when a polynomial has been completely factored.

concepts.name: Factoring Trinomials
concepts.description: Factoring trinomials of the form x² + bx + c by finding two numbers that multiply to c and add to b. Factoring trinomials of the form ax² + bx + c using the AC method or trial and error. Checking by expansion.

concepts.name: Factoring Special Cases
concepts.description: Difference of squares: a² - b² = (a+b)(a-b). Perfect square trinomials: a² + 2ab + b² = (a+b)² and a² - 2ab + b² = (a-b)². Recognizing and applying these patterns to factor quickly.
